concept.title: More Than the Hurt
concept.human_truth: A repairable hurt can become so visually dominant that one painful act starts standing in for a whole person. Accountability does not erase the act; it makes it possible to see the person without denying what happened.
concept.emotional_arc: broken promise -> hurt dominates the frame -> memory is re-edited through pain -> accountability without pressure -> direct re-seeing -> whole-person recognition without erasure
concept.format_shell: Six-slide causal cinematic sequence built around obstruction and clearing: an empty chair first represents the broken promise, then blocks the view of him, and finally moves out of the emotional center while the evidence of hurt remains visible.
concept.public_send_reason: Send this when you need to say: what you did hurt me, but I am trying not to make that moment your entire identity.
concept.safety_boundary: This route is about a one-time, repairable disappointment with honest accountability. It must not be framed as advice to overlook repeated harm, cruelty, coercion, abuse, or betrayal.

slides.copy:
You disappointed me.
For a while,
that was all I saw.
slides.visual: Late-night dining room, medium-wide diagonal geography shot from Aachu's side of the table. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. Aachu sits in the lower-left at a table set for two, still and upright rather than collapsed or crying. One visibly cold, untouched second plate, a serving bowl with a settled surface, and a burned-low plain candle prove she waited. The single empty chair intended for Zuv dominates the center foreground and creates a physical barrier. Zuv has just entered through the background doorway, rain-damp and stopped mid-step when he sees the table; he is present but visually smaller than the empty chair. His phone and keys remain in his own hands for this arrival beat. Aachu looks at the empty chair, not at him. The visual must read without copy as: he promised to be here, he was not, and his absence has become the first thing she sees. Exactly two people; no restaurant, server, flowers, gifts, background people, portraits, readable clock numbers, random lettering, or melodramatic tears.
slides.emotion: the instant one absence becomes emotionally larger than the person
slides.pose: Aachu sits upright in profile with both feet grounded and hands resting separately near her own untouched plate; she looks at the empty chair. Zuv stands just inside the doorway at the same normal adult scale, one foot halted forward, shoulders lowered, gaze on Aachu and the cold table. No reaching, pointing, kneeling, embrace, apology gesture, or camera-facing pose.
slides.wardrobe: Continuous at-home wardrobe from the selected together-01.jpg anchors: Aachu white wrap shirt and blue jeans; Zuv pale-blue shirt and charcoal trousers, slightly rain-damp on arrival.
slides.props: one dining table, exactly two dining chairs with one intentionally empty, exactly two plain plates, one serving bowl, one burned-low unlabelled candle, one phone and one key set held only by Zuv
slides.background: Modest lived dining room fading into warm ivory paper; one low pendant motivates light, a dark rain-muted window adds cool edge light, no decorative clutter.
slides.continuity_lock: The cold dinner, central empty chair, doorway, table orientation, clothing, phone, and keys continue into slide 2. The same chair returns occupied on slide 4 and moved out of the central sightline on slide 6.
slides.cta_intent: The empty chair creates an immediate swipe question: what did he miss, and can she see more than the absence?

slides.copy:
Hurt can make
one moment look like
a whole person.
slides.visual: Same late-night dining room seconds later, low table-level view from just behind Aachu's right shoulder. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. The empty chair back fills the middle plane and clearly occludes part of Zuv's torso without intersecting or merging with him, so Aachu sees him through the geometry of the chair that represented his absence. Zuv is now fully inside the room. His keys already rest on a small side ledge; with one anatomically attached right hand, he deliberately places his phone face-down beside them, away from the table, while his left hand hangs open and empty at his side. He then stays beyond the chair rather than approaching or explaining with gestures. Aachu's partial profile and shoulder remain in the near foreground, her eye-line fixed through the chair slats toward him. The cold plate and burned-low candle stay visible at opposite lower corners. Camera compression makes the chair feel larger than him while keeping clear depth separation. No reflection, extra person, bouquet, apology note, speech bubble, readable clock, or random text.
slides.emotion: hurt flattening a whole person into the shape of one broken promise
slides.pose: Aachu remains seated, visible only in clean partial profile and shoulder; no visible hands are required. Zuv stands beyond the chair, right hand placing the phone beside keys already on the ledge, left hand open and empty at his side, shoulders lowered and still. The chair is physically between them; nobody touches it or each other.
slides.wardrobe: Same clothing and rain-damp state as slide 1.
slides.props: same empty chair, same cold plate and burned-low candle, one key set already resting on the side ledge and one phone now being placed face-down beside it
slides.background: Same dining-room geography, pendant light and rain-muted window; shallow depth of field used for emotional compression, never fog or fantasy effects.
slides.continuity_lock: The phone and keys change from held on slide 1 to set away on slide 2. The empty chair remains central and unoccupied. Aachu still has not looked at Zuv without the chair between them.
slides.cta_intent: The camera makes the emotional thesis visible before the line explains it.

slides.copy:
I began judging
every memory
through that moment.
slides.visual: Later that night, a wide single-person hallway shot with exactly Aachu and no live background figure. A short row of three small framed memories sits on a narrow console. Their interiors use only soft, non-figurative washes of the couple's recurring clothing colors, with no discernible faces or bodies. Two frames are already face-down, showing only plain backs. Aachu is in the act of turning the third and final frame face-down with her right hand; her left hand stays naturally at her side. She looks at the moving frame, not toward camera. The repeated downturned rectangles create a visible action trail: one bad moment is being allowed to darken earlier memories. The dining room and Zuv are absent from view, but the cooled blue night light matches slides 1-2. Keep the action restrained and temporary, not destructive or terminal: no packed bag, removed ring, broken glass, torn paper, thrown object, crying fit, extra figure, mirror, silhouette, or random lettering.
slides.emotion: pain spreading backward through the shared archive
slides.pose: Aachu stands comfortably beside the console in three-quarter profile. Her right shoulder-to-arm-to-wrist-to-hand chain is fully visible as she rotates exactly one frame downward. Her left arm hangs naturally with the hand visible and empty. No crouching, leaning into the wall, face hiding, or theatrical distress.
slides.wardrobe: Same Aachu white wrap shirt and blue jeans; hair and jewelry stay consistent with selected identity references.
slides.props: one narrow hallway console and exactly three small memory frames: two already face-down and one being turned face-down; the visible front contains only abstract color washes with no readable text, faces, or figures
slides.background: Quiet home hallway with cool window spill and one dim wall light, clean ivory paper edges, no mirror or decorative photo wall.
slides.continuity_lock: All three frames end this slide face-down. Exactly one of these frames will be lifted upright by Aachu on slide 5 and remain upright on slide 6.
slides.cta_intent: The physical act of turning memory frames down proves the deepening without a collage or flashback montage.

slides.copy:
But pain knows
what happened,
not everything about you.
slides.visual: Following morning, over-Aachu-shoulder view from the dining-room doorway. Exactly Aachu and Zuv. Aachu is a partial foreground shoulder and cheek, stopped at the threshold but not hidden. Zuv now sits in the once-empty dining chair at the table, fully visible rather than occluded by its back. The cold plate and burned-out candle remain untouched between them as factual evidence of the previous night; he has not cleared the scene, replaced it with gifts, or staged a grand apology. His phone and keys remain face-down on the distant side ledge. He sits with both feet grounded, hands open and separate on his own thighs, eyes raised to Aachu, waiting rather than reaching. Soft neutral morning window light removes the hard chair-shadow geometry from slide 2. No breakfast makeover, flowers, gift, written apology, kneeling, tears, touch, smile, background person, or live reflection.
slides.emotion: the hurt remains documented while the person becomes visible again
slides.pose: Zuv sits naturally in the same chair with full face, hair, beard, torso, knees, and hands readable for identity evaluation. Both palms rest open on separate thighs with attached wrists and forearms. Aachu remains partially visible at the doorway with no hand or comforting action shown. Their eye-line connects across clear space.
slides.wardrobe: Same continuous wardrobe, naturally rumpled from the night; no costume or styling change.
slides.props: same chair now occupied by Zuv, same cold dinner plate and burned-out candle, same phone and key set face-down on the side ledge
slides.background: Same dining-room geography with neutral morning light; the evidence remains while the visual obstruction clears.
slides.continuity_lock: Chair state changes from empty/obstructing on slides 1-2 to occupied/fully revealing Zuv. Cold dinner remains. Aachu has not yet entered or touched any memory frame.
slides.cta_intent: The scene adds the accountability condition the copy alone cannot show: he stays present without forcing repair.

slides.copy: So I looked at you again.
slides.emotion: the first unblocked look after hurt
slides.visual: EDIT-TARGET COMPOSITION LOCK: rebuild the supplied failed proof as a table-across medium two-shot, not a side-by-side portrait. In the same sparse morning dining room, Aachu sits on the left side of a small rectangular table and Zuv sits on the opposite right side; a clearly visible strip of tabletop and open conversational distance separate their torsos. Frame both people from head through lap, with exactly Aachu and Zuv and all four hands fully visible. Low at the center foreground on the tabletop, place one genuinely palm-sized memory frame with no easel or kickstand. Freeze the physical action midway: the frame's bottom edge remains visibly planted on the tabletop, the frame plane is tilted only about forty-five degrees above the table, its plain blank back faces the viewer, and Aachu's attached right fingertips support one side edge. Her left hand stays open on her own thigh. Zuv sits upright opposite, both open hands separate on his own thighs, without reaching or leaning. Aachu has just moved her eyes from the frame to Zuv; they meet a direct unobstructed eye-line with neutral closed mouths, serious-soft faces, and no smile. Preserve guarded space: no touch, romantic inward lean, cuddling, or already-reconciled pose. At the far lower-left corner show only a thin cropped rim of one cold plate—no fork, food residue, full plate, cup, or meal spread. The background is only neutral warm-ivory paper grain plus a faint non-figurative window-light wash: no plant or foliage, shelf, cabinet, books, wall art, photograph, other frame, mirror, reflection, logo, sign, or decorative object. Exactly two human depictions total. Render no lettering anywhere on skin, clothing, furniture, props, or background. The only visible text in the entire image is the exact slide line 'So I looked at you again.' and the tiny top-right brandmark '@a.storyof.two'.
slides.pose: Opposite-side table blocking with visible tabletop gap; both torsos upright and separate. Aachu's right fingertips support the small frame at forty-five degrees while its bottom edge stays on the table; her left hand is open on her thigh. Both of Zuv's open hands remain separate on his thighs. Neutral closed mouths, direct eye contact, no smile, lean, or touch.
slides.wardrobe: Exact together-01-derived morning wardrobe: Aachu in the white wrap blouse with flared sleeves and blue jeans; Zuv in the pale-blue striped button-down and charcoal trousers. No loose white button-down substitution for Aachu and no navy T-shirt for Zuv.
slides.props: one palm-sized blank-backed memory frame at forty-five degrees with bottom edge planted on the tabletop and no easel/kickstand; only a thin cropped cold-plate rim at the far lower-left; no fork, food, cup, phone, keys, or other prop
slides.background: Neutral warm-ivory paper grain and a faint abstract window-light wash only; no plant/foliage, shelf, cabinet, books, photograph, framed art, wall frame, mirror, reflection, symbol, logo, sign, or decorative object.
slides.continuity_lock: One frame changes from face-down at the end of slide 3 to upright on slide 5. The hurt evidence remains. This is the first unobstructed mutual gaze in the sequence.
slides.cta_intent: A tiny physical choice and a direct eye-line make the short line feel earned.

slides.copy:
You had disappointed me.
You were not
a disappointment.
slides.visual: Matched wide release using the same dining-room camera axis as slide 1, now in clear morning light. Exactly Aachu and Zuv and exactly two dining chairs. Aachu remains seated in her original chair. Zuv remains seated in the same once-empty chair from slides 1 and 4, but he has pulled and rotated that chair around to the adjacent side of the table, moving its back out of their sightline and leaving no third chair. Their body distance is conversational and smaller than slide 4, without a celebratory embrace. The cold plate and burned-out candle remain at the far edge of the table, proving the hurt was not erased. One memory frame stands upright near Aachu with its plain back toward the viewer; the other two stay face-down on the distant hallway console, making the ending a beginning rather than a magical restoration. Aachu speaks or listens with one relaxed hand open on the tabletop; Zuv listens with both hands visible and separate, no touching yet. Their faces are calm and fully recognizable. The image must read without copy as: the event is still part of the room, but it is no longer the only thing between them. No third chair, cleaned table, fresh meal, flowers, gifts, hug, kiss, halo light, hearts, background figure, live reflection, or instant-happy ending.
slides.emotion: recognition without denial, closeness without a false reset
slides.pose: Natural seated two-shot with exact real body proportions. Aachu and Zuv face each other across a clear diagonal, shoulders relaxed, feet grounded, no leaning over the table. Aachu's right hand rests open on the table and left hand on her lap. Zuv's hands remain visible and separate on his thighs or table edge. No touch or reconciliation pose.
slides.wardrobe: Same continuous morning wardrobe; preserve Aachu/Zuv faces, hair, beard, skin tone, body proportions, and two-inch standing height logic from the selected identity photos.
slides.props: same dining table and exactly two chairs: Aachu in her original chair and Zuv in the once-empty chair now pulled to the adjacent side; cold plate and burned-out candle still visible; one upright memory frame with plain back toward viewer; two distant face-down frames; phone and keys still inactive on the side ledge
slides.background: Same room and hallway geography in neutral morning light, warm ivory paper field, fine watercolor-and-ink linework, sparse causal details only.
slides.continuity_lock: Pays off the cover composition: obstruction clears and body distance contracts, but the evidence of hurt remains. Only one of three memory frames is upright, preserving emotional honesty.
slides.cta_intent: The final image turns the line into a sendable truth without excusing the act or forcing instant forgiveness.

copy.caption_recommended:
I did not need the hurt to become smaller.

I needed it to stop becoming your whole face.

That took honesty. An apology that did not hurry me. And time.

Looking at you again was not forgetting what happened. It was remembering that what happened and who you are were not the same sentence.

This is for the hurts that can be repaired—not the ones that keep asking you to survive them.
copy.caption_alt: The hurt stayed true. It just stopped being the only truth I could see.
copy.posting_note: Keep the public framing explicitly about repairable hurt with accountability. Do not position this as a reason to remain in repeated harm, cruelty, coercion, abuse, or betrayal.

visual_setup: CINEMATIC CAUSAL SEQUENCE, not six poster illustrations. Locked illustrative incident: Zuv promised to be home for a simple dinner Aachu prepared and arrived after the food had gone cold. The one empty dining chair is the wound object. A short row of face-down framed memories is the memory-state object. Visual variables progress across the deck: obstruction clears and body distance contracts, while the cold dinner remains as evidence so repair never reads as erasure. Slides 1-2 stay in the dining room on the late night of the broken promise. Slide 3 moves into the hallway later that night. Slides 4-6 return to the dining room the following morning. Camera grammar progresses from a medium-wide geography shot, to a low obstructed POV, to a single-person hallway wide, to an over-shoulder accountability frame, to an eye-line close, to a matched wide release. Motivated light progresses from one low dining pendant and cooled window blue to neutral morning light. Every frame contains exactly the authorized people, no background figures or live-looking reflections. The exact on-image text stays in generous upper-middle ivory paper space. The image must add behavior and subtext; no crying close-up, apology bouquet, hug, kneeling, saintly rescue, or instant forgiveness.
